evidence.claim: A Quezon City RTC officer certified there was no record showing Marcos Jr. had satisfied the court's order to settle tax deficiencies and pay the fine after his tax-evasion conviction; the article also says his spokesperson claimed compliance but would not provide the payment details.
evidence.title: QC court certifies Bongbong Marcos didn’t pay tax dues, fines
evidence.excerpt: A Quezon City RTC officer certified there was no record showing Marcos Jr. had satisfied the court's order to settle tax deficiencies and pay the fine after his tax-evasion conviction; the article also says his spokesperson claimed compliance but would not provide the payment details.
evidence.source_locator: Lines 119-123 and 140-168 in the article text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a named court certification with explicit quotations from the spokesperson and petitioners' lawyers.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 background that remained directly relevant to the 2022 integrity question because the tax-compliance issue was still unresolved as he entered office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Marcos Jr.'s own tax obligations and his spokesperson's response; strong personal nexus.
contrary_evidence: The article is reporting a certification, not a new adjudication of guilt.

evidence.claim: In a CNN Philippines interview, Marcos Jr. denied using troll farms, saying he had been offered a click army but did not use it and insisting there were no trolls.
evidence.title: Trolls? ‘Show me one, they don’t exist’ – Marcos Jr.
evidence.excerpt: In a CNN Philippines interview, Marcos Jr. denied using troll farms, saying he had been offered a click army but did not use it and insisting there were no trolls.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted passage in the article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct quotation from Marcos Jr. in a contemporary interview, reported by a major outlet.
evidence.period_fit: April 2022 campaign period, squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal statement by Marcos Jr.
contrary_evidence: Later fact-checking and other reporting contradict the denial.
The statement alone does not prove authorship of every online account.

evidence.claim: The fact-check says Marcos Jr.'s denial of troll farms is false, citing studies, investigations, and testimony; it also notes more than 300 Marcos-linked Twitter accounts were suspended in January 2022 for platform manipulation and spam.
evidence.title: Hindi raw involved si Ferdinand Marcos Jr. sa mga troll farm?
evidence.excerpt: The fact-check says Marcos Jr.'s denial of troll farms is false, citing studies, investigations, and testimony; it also notes more than 300 Marcos-linked Twitter accounts were suspended in January 2022 for platform manipulation and spam.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Election fact-checking project with explicit reasoning and named supporting facts; strong corroborative value even though it is not a court finding.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Marcos Jr.'s public denial and to accounts linked to his campaign ecosystem.
contrary_evidence: The fact-check is not a judicial finding.
Some support is inferential through linked accounts and investigations rather than a single direct confession.

evidence.claim: The country report says Marcos held professional journalists in low regard during the campaign, barred them from campaign events, snubbed media-hosted debates, and favored friendly influencers and a partisan TV station; it also notes vilification of journalists and fact-checkers and DDoS attacks on newsrooms.
evidence.title: Philippines
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
evidence.excerpt: The country report says Marcos held professional journalists in low regard during the campaign, barred them from campaign events, snubbed media-hosted debates, and favored friendly influencers and a partisan TV station; it also notes vilification of journalists and fact-checkers and DDoS attacks on newsrooms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable annual research report with specific, time-bound observations and multiple corroborating examples.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022 campaign-period evidence, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct campaign behavior by Marcos Jr. is reported alongside attacks by third parties; attribution is strongest for the campaign access choices and media treatment.
contrary_evidence: Some of the abuse described was carried out by third parties, not Marcos personally.
The report also shows an active fact-checking and media response ecosystem.

evidence.claim: PCIJ found that Marcos Jr.'s successful 2022 campaign was funded by kin of his father's supporters and by business interests, including owners of firms barred by law from political contributions; it says 67 donors contributed P624.7 million and that Anton Lagdameo's party donation was later followed by his appointment as Special Assistant to the President.
evidence.title: Marcos return to Malacañang funded by donors linked to father’s ‘cronies’, gov’t contractors
evidence.excerpt: PCIJ found that Marcos Jr.'s successful 2022 campaign was funded by kin of his father's supporters and by business interests, including owners of firms barred by law from political contributions; it says 67 donors contributed P624.7 million and that Anton Lagdameo's party donation was later followed by his appointment as Special Assistant to the President.
evidence.source_locator: Lines 81-87, 104-107, 120-123, and 180-185 in the article text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Deep investigative report grounded in Comelec declarations and public records, with explicit discussion of legal loopholes and post-election appointments.
evidence.period_fit: Fully within the 2022 campaign and transition period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct campaign-finance nexus to Marcos Jr. and his immediate governing circle; some donor conduct is indirect but the appointment link is specific.
contrary_evidence: The article notes contributions were routed through individuals, exploiting a legal loophole.
It does not itself prove quid pro quo or illegal influence.

evidence.claim: Marcos said he chose Anton Lagdameo as Special Assistant to the President because they had worked together for the past decade and Lagdameo knew him very well.
evidence.title: Bongbong Marcos Jr. picks ex-solon Anton Lagdameo as Special Assistant to the President
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said he chose Anton Lagdameo as Special Assistant to the President because they had worked together for the past decade and Lagdameo knew him very well.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted remarks in the article body and headline
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous reporting of Marcos's own stated rationale for a sensitive appointment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct appointment choice by Marcos Jr.
contrary_evidence: The justification is familiarity and trust, not merit alone.
The appointee was also linked by PCIJ to campaign finance and donor networks.

evidence.claim: The article lists the incoming cabinet and notes that Marcos selected several experienced professionals for key roles, including Diokno, Balisacan, Medalla, Pascual, Pangandaman, Bonoan, and others; it also notes campaign manager Benhur Abalos, Sara Duterte, Enrile, and Tulfos-linked appointments that drew political-link criticism.
evidence.title: Cabinet members, economic team joining the Marcos administration
evidence.excerpt: The article lists the incoming cabinet and notes that Marcos selected several experienced professionals for key roles, including Diokno, Balisacan, Medalla, Pascual, Pangandaman, Bonoan, and others; it also notes campaign manager Benhur Abalos, Sara Duterte, Enrile, and Tulfos-linked appointments that drew political-link criticism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with a concrete roster of appointees and their prior experience, plus explicit notes on politically connected choices.
evidence.period_fit: Immediate transition and first day of office in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct appointment choices by Marcos Jr.; mixed because it contains both professional and political selections.
contrary_evidence: Several appointees were political allies or campaign figures, not technocrats.
A positive reading of competence does not by itself rule out favoritism.

evidence.claim: PFP reported P272 million in campaign spending, filed a 400-page SOCE, and said the document was signed by Anton Lagdameo, who Marcos had already chosen as Special Assistant to the President.
evidence.title: Bongbong Marcos party declares P272-M campaign spending in Eleksyon 2022
evidence.excerpt: PFP reported P272 million in campaign spending, filed a 400-page SOCE, and said the document was signed by Anton Lagdameo, who Marcos had already chosen as Special Assistant to the President.
evidence.source_locator: Article body describing the SOCE filing and Lagdameo's role
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A contemporaneous report of the party's official disclosure filing, with identifiable figures and a public record trail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly linked to Marcos's party and his incoming chief aide; the disclosure itself is official, though the article is secondary reporting.
contrary_evidence: The article frames the amount as below the legal spending ceiling.
Official disclosure does not establish donor purity or absence of influence.

evidence.claim: Marcos's first executive order abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and transferred its powers to the Office of the Deputy Executive Secretary for Legal Affairs, citing streamlining and avoidance of duplicative functions.
evidence.title: Executive Order No. 1, s. 2022
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's first executive order abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and transferred its powers to the Office of the Deputy Executive Secretary for Legal Affairs, citing streamlining and avoidance of duplicative functions.
evidence.source_locator: Section 1 of Executive Order No. 1, s. 2022
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential order; the only limitation is that the page itself was hard to render, so the search-result text was used as the quote source.
evidence.period_fit: Exactly the first day of the Marcos presidency in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential act by Marcos Jr.
contrary_evidence: The EO gives an efficiency rationale rather than an explicit anti-accountability rationale.
It abolishes PACC, not the PCGG that handles Marcos-family wealth cases.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
